title: Hosted API econ microsim playbook
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a lightweight request-level microsimulation and an accompanying spreadsheet layout to estimate hosted API unit economics (COGS and margin) by model and region. The microsim is intentionally practical: it should fit into a single Google Sheet tab + a small sample data tab and produce scenario pivot tables for product and finance reviews.

Why a microsim (vs only aggregate sheets):
- Captures non-linear effects of batching, cache hits, and latency buckets on per-token cost.
- Lets us model fallback routing (e.g., low-latency replica -> cheaper regional variant) and the knock-on effects on capacity utilization.
- Easy to extend with new samples (e.g., quantization, new GPU SKUs).

High-level approach:
1) Input sheets: workload-profile, model-profiles, region-prices, routing-policies, experiment-params.
2) Microsim engine (spreadsheet formulas / simple Apps Script or Python) samples N synthetic requests from workload-profile, applies routing + caching + batching heuristics, computes cost per request and aggregates.
3) Output sheets: per-request sample table, per-model-region COGS heatmap, per-latency-slab margin table, sensitivity pivot.

Minimum fields (sheet columns) for the "sample requests" tab: 
- request_id (string)
- model_family (gpt-4x-lite / rw-axiom / rw-compact)
- region (us-west1 / eu-west1 / ap-south1)
- prompt_tokens (int)
- generated_tokens (int)
- total_tokens = prompt_tokens + generated_tokens (formula)
- latency_sla_target_ms (int)
- chosen_route (hosted-primary / fallback-regional / dedicated-pool)
- cache_hit (yes/no)
- effective_tokens_billed (formula: total_tokens * (cache_hit? cache_billed_frac : 1))
- batch_group_id (generated by batching heuristic)
- batch_size_for_req (lookup aggregated batch size)
- per_request_gpu_seconds (formula using model throughput conditioned on batch_size)
- per_request_gpu_cost (per_request_gpu_seconds * region_gpu_hourly_rate / 3600)
- infra_overhead_share (flat or token-weighted share of infra/egress/instance overhead)
- total_cogs_usd (sum of gpu_cost + infra_overhead_share + storage/kv-cost-slice)

Key formulas and assumptions (starter numbers, editable in inputs sheet):
- GPU hourly costs by region: us-west1_p4 = $3.60/hr, eu-west1_p4 = $4.10/hr, ap-south1_p4 = $4.50/hr (editable).
- Throughput tokens/sec by model at batch=1/8/32 (example): rw-compact: [300, 1200, 3200], rw-axiom: [120, 480, 1200], gpt-4x-lite: [40, 160, 420].
- Cache billed fraction on hit = 0.12 (i.e., billed tokens = 12% of request tokens when KV prefix cache satisfied).
- Average extra infra overhead (routing, network, orchestration) per request = $0.00006 (tunable).
- Quantized runtime premium/discount: float32 vs int8 runtime multiplier (e.g., int8 = 0.7x GPU time).
- Batch efficiency curve: per-token GPU_seconds scales roughly as base_time_per_token / batch_speedup_factor(batch_size). Use empirical vectors in model_profiles tab.

Batching heuristic (spreadsheet-friendly):
- Group requests by model_family + region + latency_sla_target_ms bucket (0-150ms, 150-350ms, >350ms).
- For each group and simulated time-slice (10ms window) compute expected batch_size = Poisson(mean_rps * slice_window) truncated at model max batch.
- Assign batch_group_id and compute batch_size_for_req = average batch size for that group and window.

Caching rules:
- Two-layer cache modeled: prefix KV cache (highly selective) and session KV cache (longer-lived).
- Input sheet sets prefix_hit_rate_by_customer_segment and session_hit_rate. Microsim assigns cache hits by sampling from these rates per request.
- Hit => effective_tokens_billed = total_tokens * prefix_billed_frac (0.12), else billed = total_tokens.

Routing / fallback policy examples (configurable):
- Policy A (latency-first): route to nearest low-latency pool; if no capacity, fallback to regional cheaper variant with 1.3x latency multiplier.
- Policy B (cost-first): attempt cheaper model variant if estimated total latency < SLA.
- Microsim toggles policies per scenario to show marginal COGS and latency violations.

Output metrics to compute and visualize in sheet: 
- COGS per effective token (median, p90) by (model_family, region).
- COGS per request by latency slab.
- Contribution margin per model (price - COGS) at current list price and at 10%, 30% discount levels.
- Utilization curves for each GPU fleet by simulated minute.
- Expected outages / SLA violations under surge scenarios (e.g., 3x RPS spike).

Monte Carlo / sensitivity knobs (spreadsheet-driven):
- N_samples (5000 as default).
- Cache_hit_vars (low/expected/high).
- Batchable_fraction (percent of requests that can be batched).
- Quantization adoption (percent of tokens served on quantized runtime).
- Region_price_shocks (+/- 20%).

Quick worked example (toy numbers):
- Single sample: gpt-4x-lite, us-west1, total_tokens=800, cache_hit=no, batch_size=8.
- Throughput for gpt-4x-lite at batch=8 = 160 tokens/sec => per_request_gpu_seconds = 800 / 160 = 5s.
- GPU cost = 5s * ($3.60/hr / 3600s) = 5 * $0.001 = $0.005.
- infra_overhead_share = $0.00006 => total_cogs_usd = $0.00506 => COGS_per_token = $0.00506 / 800 = $0.000006325.

Actionable recommendations (starter list):
1) Ship a minimal "microsim" tab and a sample 1k request dump for the next finance sync. Keep all knobs at top of sheet.
2) Run 3 baseline scenarios: conservative (low batching, low cache), expected, optimistic (higher batch, 30% quantization). Capture COGS delta.
3) Build a focused experiment: enable session prefix caching for a cohort of 10 mid-size customers and measure real hit rates and latency impact (2-week A/B).
4) Implement a routing policy experiment in staging that routes <150ms SLA traffic to low-latency pool and routes >350ms SLA to cheaper variants; measure real request distributions and cost savings.
5) Integrate microsim outputs into the Console per-route cost dashboards (daily refresh).

Open questions / items to resolve: 
- Infra overhead attribution model: token-weighted vs flat per-request. We should test both and show differences.
- How to price-bucket multi-model calls (tool-calling) where single request touches more than one model family.
- Good defaults for throughput vectors for new models (we need a short onboarding checklist for model owners to provide these).

Next steps and owners: 
- Priya: prototype the sheet + sample script (2 days).
- Luca: prepare 1k synthetic request dump and baseline scenario configs (1 day).
- Evan: wire linked_sheet -> Console ingestion mapping (3 days).
- Sara: design A/B for prefix cache experiment and coordinate with infra (1 week).

Notes on reproducibility and auditability:
- All assumptions MUST be recorded in the inputs tab with a short justification and link to the benchmark run (bench id).
- Version the sheet when changing major knobs and write a 3-line changelog at the top.

Appendix: suggested sheet tabs and layout (order in file):
- README (top-level assumptions & changelog)
- inputs (region prices, model throughput vectors, overheads, batch curves)
- workload_profile (token distributions, rps by customer segment)
- sample_requests (N sampled requests, per-request outputs)
- agg_outputs (pivot tables for COGS/margin by model+region)
- sensitivity_runs (grid of runs + summar y)
- experiments (tracking A/B results)

End of doc.

(Notes: this file is a working draft; please comment on the inputs sheet layout before I build the sample script.)
